source: NCERT Class VII, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, History Ch. 5.

sections.heading: 1. Sacred Geography
points: Across India, certain **rivers, mountains, forests and places** are regarded as **sacred** — together they form a **'sacred geography'** that links the whole land.
**Tirtha** = a sacred place of pilgrimage (literally a 'ford' or crossing); **tirtha-yatra** = pilgrimage.
Pilgrimage made people **travel across regions**, weaving a shared culture.

sections.heading: 2. Sacred Rivers, Mountains and Groves
points: **Rivers** are revered — the **Ganga, Yamuna, Sarasvati**; their meeting (**sangam/Prayag**) is especially holy (site of the **Kumbh Mela**).
**Mountains** are sacred — **Kailash**, the Himalayas, and many hill shrines.
**Sacred groves** — patches of forest protected on religious grounds — help **conserve biodiversity**.

sections.heading: 3. Networks of Holy Sites
points: **Char Dham** — **Badrinath (N), Dwarka (W), Puri (E), Rameshwaram (S)** — link the four directions.
**Twelve Jyotirlingas** (Shiva) and **Shakti Peethas** (the Goddess) are spread across the land.
Great pilgrimage centres: **Varanasi (Kashi), Prayagraj, Ujjain, Nashik, Haridwar** (the Kumbh cities).

sections.heading: 4. Many Faiths, Shared Land
points: Sacred sites belong to **all of India's faiths**:

sub: **Islamic** — the **dargah of Moinuddin Chishti at Ajmer**.

points: This shared sacred geography expresses India's **unity in diversity**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Tirtha = pilgrimage site; tirtha-yatra = pilgrimage; sacred geography links the land.
Sacred rivers: Ganga, Yamuna, Sarasvati; sangam/Prayag → Kumbh Mela; sacred mountain: Kailash.
Char Dham: Badrinath (N), Dwarka (W), Puri (E), Rameshwaram (S); 12 Jyotirlingas; Shakti Peethas.
Kumbh cities: Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, Nashik.
Multi-faith sites: Bodh Gaya/Sarnath (Buddhist), Shravanabelagola/Palitana (Jain), Golden Temple (Sikh), Ajmer dargah (Islamic).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Char Dham** directions: Badrinath = north, Dwarka = west, Puri = east, Rameshwaram = south.
**Bodh Gaya** = enlightenment; **Sarnath** = first sermon — both Buddhist.
**Sacred groves** help **conserve biodiversity** (protected forest patches).
The **Kumbh Mela** rotates among **Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik**.
